transcript.text: Samsung RS68A8820S9/EU flashing 22E on the display and the fridge side isn't as cold as it should be. What does 22E mean and can I fix it?

On Samsung fridge-freezers, code 22E typically indicates a problem with the fridge evaporator fan—either the fan isn't spinning because it's stuck on ice, or the motor has failed. This stops cold air from circulating into the fridge section, which is why that side feels warm. To narrow this down: is the freezer compartment still freezing properly, or is it warming up too? If the freezer is fine but the fridge is warm, it points to an airflow issue (fan or ice blockage). If both are warm, we need to look at other cooling components.
Freezer is fine, still freezing properly. Fridge side is reading 9C and there's very little airflow from the vents. No burning smell or tripping anything, if that matters.

Since the freezer is still cold but the fridge is warm with little airflow, this suggests the cooling system is working but the cold air isn't reaching the fridge. Code 22E on Samsung models usually points to the evaporator fan not spinning correctly—either because it's jammed by ice or the motor has failed. The most common cause for a sudden blockage is ice building up behind the back panel, often due to a blocked defrost drain. To distinguish between a simple ice block and a dead motor: please unplug the fridge for 24 hours with both doors open to let all internal ice melt completely. After that time, plug it back in and listen carefully at the back of the freezer compartment: can you hear a faint whirring or humming sound from the fan area when the compressor runs? Also, check if there is any water pooling at the bottom of the fridge section.
Ok, I can do that. I've got a lot of food in there but I have a cool box. Is there anything else I should check while it's defrosting?

Yes, while it is unplugging and defrosting, keep an eye on the bottom of the fridge section. Look for any standing water or ice around the small drain hole at the back; if you see water pooling there, it suggests the defrost drain was blocked before this started, which often leads to the fan getting iced up. Also, once the 24 hours are up and you plug it back in, listen carefully for that faint whirring from the freezer area when the compressor runs—that will tell us if the fan is actually spinning again or if it's still stuck/dead.

candidates: Fridge evaporator fan fault (stuck or failed) (high)
Ice blockage in the air duct caused by a defrost system failure (medium)
